historical_references.reference: The name Devaapi is derived from the Sanskrit term Deva (god) and Aapi (mother of the gods). According to Hindu mythology, Devaapi is considered to be the mother of the gods, particularly in the context of the Vedic pantheon.
historical_references.context: In Hindu mythology, Devaapi was often invoked in various rituals and prayers to seek the blessings of the gods, as she was believed to be the source of their power and nurturing energy.

historical_references.reference: Later, in medieval Hindu texts, Devaapi was identified with the goddess Parvati, the consort of Shiva, and was worshipped as a powerful mother goddess who bestows boons and protection to her devotees.
historical_references.context: In this context, Devaapi was often depicted as a nurturing and compassionate goddess who provides comfort and relief in times of distress. Her iconography includes images of her holding a lotus or a child, signifying her maternal and protective nature.
